title: Web basics: HTML & CSS
examples: What is the difference between HTML and CSS?
How do I make text bigger on a webpage?
Can you show me how to put an image on a webpage?

explain.say: Today we learn about building web pages using HTML and CSS. HTML gives the structure to your page.
We use tags in HTML to tell the browser what something is. For example, the paragraph tag wraps text.
CSS is what helps us style the page after the structure is built. It controls the look and feel.
A concrete example is making a heading very large using CSS. We select the element and add style rules.
In a real-life example, think about a school notice board. HTML puts up the posters, and CSS makes them look colourful.
A common mistake is putting styling code directly inside HTML tags. You should keep structure and style separate.

faq.q: What is the main job of HTML?
faq.a: HTML is used to create the basic structure of a webpage. It defines the elements like headings and paragraphs.

faq.q: Can CSS change the content that HTML creates?
faq.a: Yes, CSS controls how the HTML elements look. It changes colours, sizes, and positions.
asks: Can I make text blue with CSS?

faq.q: Do I need to learn both HTML and CSS to build a website?
faq.a: Yes, you need both. HTML provides the skeleton, and CSS provides the clothing and decoration.
asks: Which one is more important first?
Can I build a site with just one?

faq.a: Tags are keywords wrapped in angle brackets, like angle brackets, that tell the browser how to display content.
asks: How do I use tags correctly?

faq.q: Where do I write my CSS code?
faq.a: You usually write CSS in a separate file that links to your HTML file. This keeps things tidy.
asks: Should I put CSS in the HTML file?
What is the best place for styling code?

facts: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.
CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.
HTML uses tags to define elements like headings and lists.
CSS uses selectors to apply styles to specific HTML elements.

quiz.say: To make text appear as a main title, which tag should you use?
quiz.why: The h1 tag is specifically designed for the most important main heading on a page.

wrong.0: This tag does not exist in standard HTML structure.
wrong.2: Paragraph tags are for blocks of regular text, not main titles.
wrong.3: The title tag only appears in the browser tab, not on the page itself.

quiz.say: If you want all your main headings to be red, what is the correct CSS rule?
quiz.why: This rule correctly selects all h1 elements and sets their color property to red.

wrong.0: The order of selector and property is incorrect for CSS syntax.
wrong.1: The curly braces must follow the selector, not precede it.
wrong.2: CSS requires a property name followed by a colon and a value.

quiz.say: Which combination correctly structures a list of items?
quiz.why: The unordered list tag, ul, contains list items, li, which correctly structures the points.

wrong.0: The list item tags need to wrap the content, not just the first item.
wrong.2: Using multiple separate <list> tags is not the correct way to group list items.
wrong.3: The list items need to be wrapped inside a parent container like <ul>.
